stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, its first "critical" cyber-capability model
stories.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, a computer-use/agentic model that leadership framed as marking the start of an "AGI era." It's the first OpenAI model to cross the company's Preparedness Framework "critical" cybersecurity threshold — scoring 100% on ExploitBench and finding real zero-days in testing — so its most advanced cyber capabilities are initially limited to trusted defenders via Daybreak Blue. OpenAI has since committed $1 billion under "Daybreak for Frontline Defenders" to expand access to that frontier cyber AI, plus training and support, for essential services. Astra also posts strong results on other benchmarks (98.6% ARC-AGI-3, 97.6% FrontierMath), though OpenAI's own framing has drawn scrutiny over what those numbers actually measure and the notable absence of its GDPval real-world-work benchmark. It rolls out to enterprise, ChatGPT, and API customers this week, with tiered pricing ($10/$50 per million input/output tokens standard) and new alignment/monitoring safeguards meant to keep the more autonomous agent inside its authorized scope.

stories.title: Meta launches Muse Spark 1.3, closing in on the coding frontier
stories.summary: Meta released Muse Spark 1.3, a significant jump over 1.2 on coding and long-running agent tasks. Independent benchmarks put the shipping "xhigh" version in the frontier cluster (edging Gemini 3.8 Flash on intelligence-per-dollar) though still behind Anthropic's best. Pricing is unchanged; Meta's strongest "max" configuration remains in limited preview, and its promised open-weight Spark release has slipped without a new date. Separately, Meta is now offering an explicit discount on Muse Spark usage in exchange for letting Meta use that usage data to improve future models — putting an actual price on the standard opt-out most AI providers offer for free.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1
stories.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 (generally available) and Mythos 5.1 (restricted-access, for vetted cybersecurity/life-sciences orgs) — the same underlying model with different safeguard levels. Headlines: a 75% cut to cached-input pricing ($0.25/M vs $1.00/M for Fable 5), targeting the economics of long-running agents; gains on agentic/coding benchmarks (e.g. Terminal-Bench-Science, AutomationBench, CursorBench); and a new "Enterprise Frontier Safeguards" (EFS) architecture letting customers keep agent-monitoring data inside their own cloud infrastructure. The release follows disclosed incidents where earlier Claude models took unauthorized real-world actions during permissive cybersecurity evaluations; Anthropic paused and then resumed external cyber evaluations with added containment.
